items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: Jules Cassard played trombone, yeah. Right? That's the same one? Yeah. That's his cousin. His uncle. His uncle, yeah.

ctx.x: He said Jules Cassard played trombone.

Jules Cassard played trombone, yeah. Right? That's the same one? Yeah. That's his cousin. His uncle. His uncle, yeah. Jules played trombone, yeah. He played trombone, yeah. He got songwriters in the family. I see you. Talk about a sweet barricone, that song could play a sweet barricone too. And you ought to see him on the piano too. Everything is well accompanied. And he played a violin, played a wonderful guitar. He played trombone. Did he go away with no Jews? No. The Jews went away a long time ago. I thought…
You were talking about this drummer, that's the Frisco, the drummer? And Ragbag Stevens in that old time.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: Jules and I all keep together.

ctx.x: Yes. Yes. He travels with the races or something.

That's what I would, yeah. Yeah. Somebody's on. Jules and I all keep together. Started out Jules Casdard. Henry Brunas. Well, Henry came after. He was here. Eddie Edwards. And what's his name that died? Yellow Lunez. Remember what? Yellow Lunez.
I've got lots of his records.
